name: Yasawa Islands
tagline: Island chain north of the Mamanucas with limestone sea caves and a coral lagoon
description: The Yasawas are an island chain north of the Mamanuca Islands. Sawa-i-Lau has limestone sea caves that visitors swim into, one reached through an underwater passage. Nanuya Lailai has a coral beach known as the Blue Lagoon, near where the 1980 film The Blue Lagoon was shot, and a fish sanctuary to snorkel. Waya Lailai has a peak that visitors climb for sunrise.
whyVisit: Climb a volcanic peak for sunrise

goodToKnow.title: Caves are a boat trip
goodToKnow.detail: Sawa-i-Lau's caves are reached by boat and swum into, one through an underwater passage.

goodToKnow.title: Blue Lagoon is a day-trip beach
goodToKnow.detail: Day trips visit the Blue Lagoon beach on Nanuya Lailai. The original lagoon from the film is privately owned.

goodToKnow.title: Climb Waya Lailai at sunrise
goodToKnow.detail: Guides are available, or you can go alone. The walk can continue along the island and across the spit to Waya.

bestTimeBlurb: Visit in {months}, the cooler months, for sea caves, snorkelling and island walks. Cyclones can occur Nov to Apr.
